bindings.label: Patient presented with perianal pain worsening over four days, accompanied by overall fatigue and diminished sense of taste
Patient is a 70-year-old Chinese man with no significant past medical history; he appeared fragile but alert.

Physical examination: temperature 36.3°C, blood pressure 93/66 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/minute; digital anal examination revealed a 6×4 cm lump with obvious pressure pain, unclear border, and no necrotic skin fading detected.
Lab tests show markedly elevated CRP (247.09 mg/L) and procalcitonin (20.19 ng/mL) with neutrophilia and thrombocytopenia
Blood culture confirmed Gram-variable rods by MALDI-TOF/16S rRNA
Lactate -18.38 is implausible and likely a laboratory error
Patient has bacteremia/sepsis secondary to acute perianal abscess
Bacteremia/sepsis secondary to perianal abscess caused by anaerobic Gram-variable rods
Bacteremia/sepsis secondary to perianal abscess caused by mixed aerobic-anaerobic enteric flora
Bacteremia/sepsis secondary to perianal abscess caused by Actinomyces species
Bacteremia/sepsis secondary to perianal abscess caused by Clostridium species
Perianal imaging (ultrasound/MRI) has not been performed to confirm abscess extent
Final species identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing are still pending
Peripheral blood flow cytometry identified a clonal T-cell population comprising 18% of lymphocytes
